projectTitle: Fox Chase: A cancer center site patients can navigate
project_haiku: Fox Chase Cancer Center had years of pages and no clear way through them. With Transit Authority Figures, we rebuilt the site in Drupal so patients, researchers, and the marketing team could each find their way.
project_footer_CTA: Need a hospital site that patients can use and editors can change? We built that for Fox Chase.
pageSummary:
The job

By 2015 the Fox Chase Cancer Center site in Philadelphia had grown without a plan. Patients needed clinical services and a way to ask for an appointment. Researchers needed their programs visible. Marketing needed to tell a story without calling a developer. The center hired Transit Authority Figures for design and information architecture, and Knectar to build it in Drupal.

What we built

Rob and Damia at Transit Authority Figures designed the homepage, the listings, and the inner pages: a hero, generous type, and photography of clinicians and patients. Editors assemble pages from components, including slideshows, quotes, related stories, and lists. Search covers doctors, scientists, clinical trials, and programs, including the Google Search Appliance the center already used. Video, maps, calendars, and forms stay on their outside hosts and embed cleanly. Text can scale to 200 percent, images have alternative text, and the layout holds on a phone.

Outcomes

A patient can find a service. An editor can publish a story inside the design. The site meets the accessibility bar Temple University set for this work.
